---
title: Python plotting guide
---

Plotfoundry `0.1.0.dev1` supplies a dependency-free data core and an optional
Matplotlib adapter. It runs without R, Node, htmpres or a document engine.
[Scientific choices](plotting-packages.md) · [Browse specimens](plotting-gallery.qmd?interface=python)

## Install reviewed source

Use **Python 3.12+** in a virtual environment. Git is needed only for this
source-install recipe; pip builds the selected Python directory, not htmpres:

```sh
python3.12 -m venv .venv
# Activate the environment using your shell's usual command.
.venv/bin/python -m pip install 'plotfoundry[matplotlib] @ git+https://github.com/rahuldave/htmpres.git@7b1bff11284ad2960f984f0f8ed772fa09c06d8c#subdirectory=packages/python'
```

On Windows, use the environment's `Scripts/python.exe` instead of `.venv/bin/python`.
Nothing is being installed from a Plotfoundry PyPI release. Git/pip and network
access are setup tools; installed plotting does not invoke Git or fetch assets.

If you already downloaded the pinned repository source, build a local artifact:

```sh
python -m pip install build
python -m build /path/to/reviewed-source/packages/python --outdir dist
python -m pip install 'dist/plotfoundry-0.1.0.dev1-py3-none-any.whl[matplotlib]'
```

The source distribution rebuilds independently with bundled inputs. For an
**offline target**, prepare a wheelhouse containing the package and all selected
native dependency wheels on a compatible connected machine, transfer it, then:

```sh
python -m pip install --no-index --find-links wheelhouse 'plotfoundry[matplotlib]==0.1.0.dev1'
```

A lone wheel is not a substitute for NumPy/Matplotlib dependencies. pandas and
Seaborn are optional; install them explicitly when using their examples.

## First Matplotlib plot

```python
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from plotfoundry import theme
from plotfoundry.matplotlib import context, line, style_axes, export

style = theme("folio", mode="dark", profile="presentation", surface="paper",
              figure_width_inches=8, placed_width_css_px=1152)
with context(style):
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 4))
    line(ax, [0, 1, 2], [1, None, 3], style,
         domain=["Observed"], category="Observed")
    ax.set(title="Results", xlabel="Time", ylabel="Value")
    style_axes(ax, style)
    export(fig, style, "results", formats=["png", "svg", "pdf"], dpi=144)
    plt.close(fig)
```

The missing observation stays a gap. Supply an explicit ordered domain even when
some categories are absent. Theme selection accepts all nine family IDs from the
gallery, `light`/`dark`, `reading`/`presentation`, and `paper`/`panel`.

## Supported API

| Operation | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `load_spec()`, `theme(...)` | Native data/configuration; no Matplotlib import or global mutation |
| `rc(style)`, `context(style, overrides={...})` | Theme-only furniture; nested/error restoration and explicit overrides |
| `line(..., domain=[...], category=...)` | Opaque line/ink under-stroke, shared dash geometry, edged markers and direct labels |
| `scatter(..., domain=[...], categories=[...])` | Explicit category identities, shapes/edges and labels |
| `colorscale(style, vmin=..., vmax=..., kind="sequential")` | Exact sampled map and explicit normalization |
| `colorscale(..., kind="diverging", center=...)` | Exact center and asymmetric arms |
| `scatter_values(...)` | Continuous points, exact map/norm; missing points omitted |
| `heatmap(...)` | Explicit numeric cell colors and crossed missing cues |
| `style_axes(ax, style)`, `annotate(..., role="body_annotation")` | Rebind supported native furniture and late-created text |
| `export(...)` | Fixed canvas, exact-file text checks and PNG/SVG/PDF reports |

Unknown/duplicate/over-capacity domains and malformed numeric inputs fail before
artist mutation. `variant="colorblind-subset-5"` explicitly selects the conditional
five slots. Variant changes can recolor IDs; review the mapping yourself. Dense
labels, arbitrary filled/dense marks and unsupported artists are not made compliant
by a color cycle or a global theme. Missing scatter points are omitted; there is
no separate missing-point symbol API.

## Seaborn and pandas

Use their ordinary APIs when you want native plots with furniture. That is
**theme-only** unless supported Plotfoundry helpers add the operational treatment.
For example, pass dataframe columns to `line()` with a stable domain rather than
claiming `sns.lineplot()` automatically adds under-strokes and direct labels.

```sh
python -m pip install 'pandas==3.1.1' 'seaborn==0.13.2'
python -m plotfoundry.examples.dataframes
```

The shipped example exercises `sns.lineplot`, `DataFrame.plot` and treated helper
lines separately. Late-created legends, colorbars and annotations need explicit
styling/export; no implicit guarantee applies to arbitrary Seaborn artist trees.

[Download dataframe example](_generated/plotting/source/dataframes.py)

## Fonts, placement and export

Bundled exact-file FontProperties are applied to supported text, including axes,
legend and colorbar furniture, even with a conflicting host family installed.
Only real resolved weights are used. Keep plain text: mathtext/TeX, log formatters
that introduce mathtext, or missing glyphs fail rather than claim a false font match.
Use explicit plain-text tick formatters when necessary.

`style.points(px)` applies the shared placement formula. Preserve the declared
figure width when composing it into a document. DPI is not an alternate font-size
control; `export` uses explicit dimensions without tight cropping and reports
actual PNG dimensions. SVG outlines are not editable text. PDF requests TrueType
subsets and checks structure; this is not full PDF conformance certification.
Always inspect the actual output, especially clipping, label density and downstream
SVG/PDF handling. Original font notices still apply.

## Reproduce the gallery

```sh
python -m plotfoundry.examples.gallery --case folio/dark/reading/paper --output plots
```

[Download standalone gallery source](_generated/plotting/source/python-gallery.py).
After installing the package, the downloaded equivalent runs as
`python python-gallery.py --case folio/dark/reading/paper --output plots`.
The specimen canvas is 8 × 8 inches. All 72 Python cases have PNG/SVG/PDF downloads.

Tested reference: Python 3.12.10, Matplotlib 3.11.2, NumPy 2.5.4, pandas 3.1.1,
Seaborn 0.13.2. Declared compatibility ranges are Matplotlib `>=3.11.2,<3.12` and
NumPy `>=2.5.4,<2.6`; this does not prove every future patch/platform/backend.
The development lock is verification tooling, not an installed runtime dependency.
